description: A quantizer that loads Scala scale files at random from the folder bundled with the plugin: an incoming pitch is folded into one octave and pulled to the nearest interval of the loaded scale

inputs.text: The pitch to be quantized, at a volt per octave; a polyphonic cable is quantized channel by channel

outputs.text: The quantized pitch at a volt per octave, with as many channels as the input carries

notes: The left and right arrows walk back and forth through the scales loaded so far. Pressing the right arrow when there is nothing ahead loads a fresh scale at random.
The panel's three columns are the scale's name read upward, a strip per interval with the lowest at the bottom, and that interval's size in cents.
Click an interval strip to take that interval out of the scale or put it back, and drag across several to paint a run. Grey is out of the scale, amber is in it, yellow is sounding.
The dice between the two arrows is decoration. It is drawn with no handler for a click, so pressing it does nothing; the menu's Random scale item is what rolls a new one.
Intervals you switch off are not kept. They are reset to all-on every time a scale is loaded, and only the list of scale files and the position in it are saved with the patch.
A pitch is matched only against the intervals inside its own octave, so a pitch between the top interval and the octave above is pulled down to that top interval rather than to the next root.
The arrows, the dice and the three display columns are all custom widgets rather than separate controls, so none can be clicked for help. Only the two jacks can.
The folder that ships with the plugin holds 5401 scale files, and a scale is picked from it at random the first time the module is placed.
menu: Random scale — loads another scale at random and puts it into the history directly after the one in use
Choose scala file — opens a file chooser for a .scl file; a file from outside the plugin's own scl folder is copied into it first, and files with any other extension are refused
